A1.statement: The frozen v1 forecast beat carrying day 7 forward on 28 earlier batches despite two missing inputs.

A2.statement: Abstention on predicted difficulty transferred to 28 earlier batches, for both predictors.

A2b.statement: The learned difficulty model adds value over declining extreme forecasts.

A4.statement: The v1 early-warning ranking did not beat the dose rule.

A5.statement: Intervals under-covered below the v1 bar on external batches.

B1.statement: A v2 forecaster beat carrying day 7 forward on 28 earlier batches with unseen chemicals.

B1b.note: Arm A carries a disclosed input handicap; B1b is reported but not claimed as an algorithmic improvement unless v1_refit, fit on the same release inputs, is also beaten.

B2.statement: The locked trust score ranks predictability better than the extremity rule on external batches.

B3.statement: Early warning did not beat the dose rule.

B4.statement: The day-7 decision did not reach the stated agreement or share; no recording-time saving is claimed.

arm_A_handicap: The release lacks cv.time and cv.network, so those v1 inputs are missing (the tool treats them as unobserved), and the recordings were re-processed. Measured on the spent reserve before unsealing: v1 date-macro MAE 0.7716 on the archive, 0.7904 without the two readouts, 0.8200 on the release copy; persistence 0.6088 and 0.6086; declined 32 and 33; low-reference-activity flags 84 and 84. The same handicap applies to the external test and is stated beside every Arm A forecast number.
